action: Scan the inguinal region to identify the saphenofemoral junction.
interpretation: Visualize the saphenofemoral junction anatomy.

action: Direct attention to the left side of the screen (lateral aspect of the patient).
interpretation: Identify the femoral arteries and note that they are already bifurcated (split).

action: Direct attention to the right side of the screen.
interpretation: Identify the Common Femoral Vein (CFV) and the Great Saphenous Vein (GSV).

action: Slide the probe slightly proximal from the current position.
interpretation: Relocate the view just proximal to the junction area.

action: Hold the probe steady at the proximal position.
interpretation: Re-confirm the anatomy: Common Femoral Vein is visible with two arteries on the left side of the screen.

action: Apply downward pressure to compress the vein, then release pressure.
interpretation: Assess the compressibility of the Common Femoral Vein.

action: Slide the probe slightly distal to isolate the Saphenofemoral Junction (SFJ). Apply compression, then release.
interpretation: Target the SFJ specifically to check for compressibility.

action: Slide the probe to the region of the Deep Femoral Vein and Superficial Femoral Vein confluence. Apply compression.
interpretation: Target the confluence of the deep and superficial venous systems.

action: Scan back and forth (rock/slide) to optimize the view, then compress.
interpretation: Differentiate the non-compressible arteries from the compressible veins.

action: Focus the scan on the specific confluence area.
interpretation: Identify the confluence of the Deep Femoral Vein and the Femoral Vein.

action: Apply compression directly over the Deep Femoral Vein.
interpretation: Confirm the Deep Femoral Vein collapses while noting the arteries remain non-compressible.

action: Slide the probe distally to follow the femoral vein down the thigh. Apply compression.
interpretation: Track the femoral vein distally.

action: Continue compressing the vein while sliding the probe downward.
interpretation: Note the anatomical relationship: The femoral vein is located underneath (deep to) the artery in this region.

action: Perform repetitive sequential compressions ('Again, again, again').
interpretation: Ensure continuous patency along the femoral canal.

action: Complete the scan of the inguinal and mid-thigh regions.
interpretation: Confirm the absence of DVT in the inguinal and mid-thigh anatomy.

action: Transition the probe to the popliteal fossa.
interpretation: Prepare to visualize the popliteal vein.

action: Adjust depth settings to visualize the bone cortex deep to the vessels.
interpretation: Identify the bone cortex to ensure the scan is deep enough to see deep vasculature, distinguishing it from superficial structures.

action: Apply compression in the popliteal fossa.
interpretation: Assess the popliteal vein for compressibility.

action: Observe the vessel relationship during compression.
interpretation: Identify the popliteal vein positioned on top of the artery and confirm it is fully compressible.

action: Conclude the examination.
interpretation: Confirm the patient does not have a proximal leg DVT.
